installation.note: sort is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: sort sorts lines of text files. It can sort alphabetically, numerically, by specific fields, and in reverse order. Essential for organizing data, preparing data for processing, and creating ordered lists.

syntax.description: Sort lines of FILE (or standard input). Output is sorted lines. Default is alphabetical sort.

options.use_case: Sort numbers correctly (10 comes after 9, not before 2)
Sort in descending order (Z to A, or high to low)
Sort and remove duplicates in one command
Sort by second column instead of first

breakdown.case: Uppercase comes before lowercase by default

output_explanation.notes: Sorts lines alphabetically. Output goes to stdout - original file unchanged.

elements.meaning: Numeric sort - treats values as numbers

output_explanation.notes: Sorts numbers correctly. Without -n, 10 comes before 2 (alphabetical). With -n, proper numerical order.

examples.title: Sort in reverse

elements.meaning: Reverse order - Z to A or high to low

breakdown.useful: Get largest values first, newest first, etc.

output_explanation.notes: Sorts in reverse order. Common pattern: sort -rn (reverse numeric - largest first).

examples.use_case: Sort in descending order (largest first, Z to A)

examples.title: Sort and remove duplicates
examples.description: Sort and show only unique lines

breakdown.useful: Common pattern: sort | uniq (same as sort -u)

output_explanation.notes: Sorts and removes duplicates. Equivalent to sort | uniq but more efficient.

examples.title: Sort by column

breakdown.fields: Fields separated by whitespace by default
breakdown.useful: Sort data files by specific columns

output_explanation.notes: Sorts by specified column. -k2 = second column, -k3 = third, etc. Useful for data files.

examples.use_case: Sort data files by specific columns

misconceptions.title: sort modifies files
misconceptions.reality: sort outputs to stdout by default - original file unchanged. Use sort file.txt > sorted.txt or sort -o file.txt file.txt to save.
misconceptions.tip: sort outputs to stdout. Use redirection to save: sort file.txt > sorted.txt, or sort -o file.txt file.txt to overwrite.

common_pitfalls.solution: Always use sort -n for numeric data. Without -n, numbers are sorted alphabetically (wrong order).

related_commands.relationship: Unique lines; sort often used with uniq
related_commands.description: Remove duplicate lines (often used with sort)

related_commands.relationship: Data processing; sort organizes, awk processes
related_commands.description: Process data (can sort with awk too)

best_practices: Use sort -u to remove duplicates while sorting
Combine with other commands: ls -l | sort -k5 -n (sort by size)
Use redirection to save: sort file.txt > sorted.txt
performance_tips: sort is fast for most files
Can be slow for very large files
Use sort -u instead of sort | uniq (more efficient)

additional_notes.default_behavior: sort outputs to stdout - original file unchanged. Use redirection or -o to save.
additional_notes.numeric_sort: Always use -n for numbers. Without -n, 10 comes before 2 (alphabetical order).
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: sort file (alphabetical), sort -n file (numeric), sort -rn file (reverse numeric), sort -u file (unique)
